subject: pickling and unpickling fitted pystan models

messages.author: e7773f79af9d66e4
messages.subject: pickling and unpickling fitted pystan models
parts:
Is it possible to pickle a fitted pystan model?

Following the example on this page, I was able to pickle a compiled model (and then unpickle it for later use), but I can't tell for sure if you can pickle a fitted model, too.

I tried pickling a fit instance using a pystan.StanModel object called model, a fitted model instance fit = model.sampling(...), and pickle.dump(fit,f) (where f is defined inside a with clause - see the attached file for the actual code), and the script seems to run okay (i.e., it doesn't give me an error, the model fits, files get written to the hard drive, etc...), but I can't later unpickle the fit object. I get this error (grt_lr_tt_tdsz is the model name passed in the StanModel call):

messages.author: f4c2e63aec3c6db2
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] pickling and unpickling fitted pystan models
parts:
Hi Noah,

There are model objects and fit objects. Model objects are picklable.
Pickling them is well-tested.

For fit objects, the best strategy is to pickle the output of the
fit, so `pickle.dump(fit.extract(), f)`.

That said, it is possible to pickle the entire fit object with the
caveat that you *must* have the associated model object available in the
current environment. So you could unpickle the model object and only
then unpickle the fit object. (The plan is to clean up this problem in
Stan 3.0.)

Best wishes,

Allen

In theory. I think it's safe to call this particular feature
experimental. Currently there's a lot of unavoidable coupling between
the model object and the fit object preventing things from working as
cleanly as they might.
